nodes.label: Agentlens Visual Identity: Neon Aperture and Agent Orbit Network
nodes.norm_label: agentlens visual identity: neon aperture and agent orbit network

nodes.label: Project-Qualified Session Identity
nodes.rationale: A raw transcript ID is not unique across projects, so an owning project is required to prevent silent collisions.

nodes.label: Ordered Agent Name Resolution
nodes.rationale: Unknown agent types remain analyzable so aggregate counts do not silently shrink.

nodes.label: Counted Parse Health
nodes.rationale: A wholly unusable or identity-less parse is rejected rather than represented as a partial result that callers could forget to check.

nodes.label: Qualified Session Key
nodes.rationale: Original identity components remain available because the derived key is not human-readable.

nodes.label: One Session Record Per Spawn
nodes.rationale: Session facts include sidecar fields that are not aggregations of tool invocations, so the session record is not a pure rollup.

nodes.label: Tool Invocation Record
nodes.rationale: Unmatched invocations are retained because abandoned calls signal interruption and attempted work.

nodes.label: In-Place Report Overwrite
nodes.rationale: Queryable history belongs in the store; timestamped report copies would create a divergent source of truth.

nodes.label: Output and Diagnostic Stream Separation
nodes.rationale: Warnings on the machine-readable stream would break piped consumers.

nodes.label: Unscored Spawn Coverage
nodes.rationale: Coverage consumers need rows for missing scores; omission would make incomplete analysis appear complete.

nodes.label: Fact Session Spawn Grain
nodes.rationale: The individual spawn is the unit of analysis; collapsing by agent type makes averages wrong.

nodes.label: Rebuildable Store Cache
nodes.rationale: Source reproducibility makes schema changes rebuilds rather than migrations and keeps hand-written queries affordable.

nodes.label: Snapshot Staleness and Soundness Guard
nodes.rationale: A half-read or changed-mid-read file must not degrade data previously read soundly.

nodes.label: Behavior-Preserving Refactor With No Migration
nodes.rationale: The emitted schema and on-disk representation remain unchanged, so old and new code can read each other's stores and rollback needs no data step.

nodes.label: Generated SQL Column Enumerations
nodes.rationale: Only mechanical column lists are generated; meaningful SQL skeletons and the staleness predicate remain literal and greppable.

nodes.label: Name-Keyed Row Extractor Map
nodes.rationale: Walking one declaration for both SQL and values removes positional drift; a key-set equality test makes missing extractors fail loudly.

nodes.label: Nullability and Primary-Key Style Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Normalizing key declarations would change SQLite null enforcement, violating the behavior-preserving constraint.

nodes.label: Single Column Order Declaration
nodes.rationale: An explicit ordered tuple makes order intentional and avoids coupling storage layout to reflected domain dataclass internals.

nodes.label: sqlite3.Row Name-Keyed Reads
nodes.rationale: Named access removes read dependence on column position while keeping sqlite3.Row confined to store.

nodes.label: Storage-Owned Column Definition
nodes.rationale: SQLite column definitions remain in store because driver-shaped storage details must not enter domain models.

nodes.label: Phase One Column Sequencing
nodes.rationale: The refactor lands before parent lineage and other queued columns so future additions cannot exercise the positional drift hazard.

nodes.label: Silent Column Drift Defect
nodes.rationale: Seven positional restatements can silently write same-typed counters into the wrong columns while round-trip tests still pass.

nodes.label: Store-Only Refactor Scope
nodes.rationale: The change preserves an already-shipped vertical slice while changing only the internal expression of store behavior.

nodes.label: Pre-Refactor Schema Pin Tests
nodes.rationale: Tests must pass against literal DDL before refactoring so they compare old and new behavior instead of validating the generator against itself.

nodes.label: Session Command Contract
nodes.rationale: The command qualifies identity by owning project to avoid raw transcript ID collisions and exposes failure families through stable exit codes.

nodes.label: Parser Integrity Contract
nodes.rationale: The parser preserves unmatched work and partial line health but rejects snapshots whose overall identity or revision soundness cannot be established.

nodes.label: Report Output Contract
nodes.rationale: Reports retain unscored spawns for honest coverage, isolate diagnostics from pipeable JSON, and overwrite stable artifacts to avoid a second history store.

nodes.label: Store Integrity Contract
nodes.rationale: Spawn-grain upserts accept only sound, non-stale snapshots, while the database remains a source-reproducible cache.
